producer_report.summary:
Accepted D112 and revised the records-history design. The history is now the branch `athena/records` with its own root. The design has a new §13 listing the readers of `records/`, a pre-merge up-to-date requirement in §5.1, and the three open points filled in. CHANGELOG records the acceptance. Only the three named files changed, and `cargo test --locked` passes.

The study site generator does not read `records/`. `xtask/src/site.rs` reads `studies/firstmate-work-handling`, so §13 says no job moves it. That differs from the request's list. I added walltime as a reader the request did not list.

§13 is placed after §12 to keep section numbers stable.

checks_run.note: Run as `cargo test --locked --quiet`; every test result line shows 0 failed.
Only CHANGELOG.md, docs/decisions.md and docs/design/records-history.md are modified.

criteria_check.criterion: No occurrence of `refs/athena/records` or `refs/athena/*` remains in docs/design/records-history.md or the D112 entry, except where explaining the change from the earlier custom ref. Every place that named the ref (§3 recommendation and assumption, §6.1, §7 table, §10 job 1, §12) now names the branch `athena/records` with its own root. The A4 row says a plain clone carries it.
criteria_check.evidence: Grep of records-history.md for `refs/athena` leaves only the status paragraph, the §3 why-a-branch and host-requirement text, and the §12 note, all explaining the change. The D112 entry names the old ref only in a parenthetical explaining the change. The A4 row says a plain clone carries both histories.

criteria_check.criterion: The design states why a branch: the host's branch rules can forbid force-pushes and deletion, and a plain clone carries it. The host-accepts-`refs/athena/*` assumption and its open point are replaced by the host-rules requirement.
criteria_check.evidence: §3 has a 'Why a branch' paragraph and a 'Requirement on the host' paragraph. The §12 open point is replaced by the decided list plus the host-rules note.

criteria_check.criterion: A new readers section lists each reader that reads records/ from the working tree today: status, forecasting and the reference forecaster, scoring, retry carry, audit, introspection, and the study site generator. For each it gives where it reads now (a code path found in the repository) and how it reads after the cutover, for example a worktree of athena/records at a fixed path. It names the build-plan job that moves it. The build plan in §10 is updated so some job owns this work.
criteria_check.evidence: §13 has the two seams and a table with a row per reader (status, forecasting and reference forecaster, scoring, retry carry, audit, introspection, study site generator, walltime, other Records::load callers, gate, other file readers). Each row gives the file and function from my grep, the after-cutover read and the job. The site row states that site.rs reads studies/ and that no job moves it. §10 job 7 now owns the reader move and the worktree.

criteria_check.criterion: The design states that the pre-merge status depends on the host requiring branches to be up to date before merging, so the squash's parent equals the head's base. The text names what happens if the host does not require it.
criteria_check.evidence: §5.1 step 1 'Dependency on up-to-date branches' states the dependency, the failure case (landing pending, then unattributed) and the recovery (re-verify after the merge, or a declared intervention). §3 lists it as a host requirement.

criteria_check.criterion: Open points are filled: pending window 15 minutes (§5.2 states it as the value, not an example), cutover after build job 6, and two weeks between job 7 and job 8. §10 and §12 are consistent with these; §4 and §12 no longer leave these points open.
criteria_check.evidence: §5.2 says 'a bounded window of 15 minutes'. §4 and §10 say C0 is chosen after job 6 and job 7 is the cutover. §4, §10 and §11 say two weeks between job 7 and job 8. §12 lists them as decided.

criteria_check.criterion: The design's Status line and D112 in docs/decisions.md say accepted, citing the BRIEF.md addenda of 2026-10-23. D112's Decision, Tradeoff and Provenance text uses the branch name and no longer says 'proposed' or 'not accepted'.
criteria_check.evidence: Status line: 'accepted, design only (D112), under Sri's delegation in the BRIEF.md addenda of 2026-10-23'. D112 Decision begins 'Accepted' and uses `athena/records`. Tradeoff and Provenance were rewritten. A grep of decisions.md found no 'Proposed' or 'not accepted' wording in the D112 entry.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry recording the acceptance and the three changes. The existing entry that says 'Awaiting Sri's decision' is updated or superseded. git diff shows changes only in docs/design/records-history.md, docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md.
criteria_check.evidence: The old entry now drops 'proposed' and 'Awaiting Sri's decision'. A new entry records the acceptance, the three changes and the filled values. `git status --short` lists exactly three modified files.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `git status` and `git diff --stat`: only those three paths changed. Run `cargo test` and confirm it passes, in case a test validates decisions.md format.
criteria_check.evidence: `git status --short` shows only the three paths. `cargo test --locked --quiet` shows every result line with 0 failed. I did not run `git diff --stat` separately.

open_issues: I could not read the BRIEF.md addenda of 2026-10-23 and cited them as the request gives them.
Readers are grouped by seam, with the minor Records::load callers in one row rather than one row each.
Whether the host supports a rule requiring branches to be up to date is not visible from code. The design states it as a requirement checked in job 1.
I did not run fmt or clippy because the change is docs-only; Athena will run them.
mistakes: I first wrote 'readers in §9', then moved the readers to a new §13 to avoid renumbering, and corrected the header reference to §13.
The §4 reference '(§9)' to the build plan was already wrong; I corrected it to §10.
learnings: Readers of records/ go through two seams: Records::load and RecordSet::load take a git treeish, and introspect::read_records and xtask walltime take a filesystem root.
labeled.rs and steward.rs also read files under records/.
The Bash hook rejects `tail`, so cargo output must be shrunk with --quiet. Files outside the working directory cannot be read.
desires: Read access to BRIEF.md addenda of 2026-10-23 to quote them exactly.
